details.failoverHelp: Both keys publish into the same room, so the player URL is identical. Point a redundant/failover encoder at the backup key and keep it on standby — if the primary drops, start the backup and the channel stays live with no URL change.
details.passthroughHelp: Push H.264/AAC to the RTMP URL (port :1937) and play it from the HLS/player URL. There is no WebRTC, recording or room features on this endpoint.
details.srtLatency: SRT adds a ~{{ms}} ms receive-latency budget (UDP retransmission window) on top of the HLS latency.
details.srtHelp: Push H.264/AAC over SRT (UDP) to the URL above. The stream key travels as ?streamid= in the URL — the key IS the credential, no user/password applies. Play it from the HLS/player URL.
details.mpegtsHelp: This ingress PULLS an MPEG-TS stream from the udp:// source above (a multicast group or a unicast port) and remuxes it straight to HLS. There is no push URL or stream key — the source IS the input. Play it from the HLS/player URL.

create.title: Create ingress
create.urlHint: Required for URL type. rtsp://, rtmp:// and http(s):// sources — srt:// is accepted too (LiveKit PULLS the remote SRT source; needs a LiveKit server version with SRT support).
create.transcodeHint: Required for RTMP/URL; optional for WHIP.
create.backupHint: Also mint a second RTMP key into the same room for encoder redundancy. Same player URL.

passthrough.title: Passthrough (remux, no transcode)
passthrough.hint: Remux the RTMP straight to HLS (ffmpeg -c copy) on port :1937, bypassing LiveKit. Near-zero CPU, no GPU — but source must be H.264/AAC.
passthrough.warningTitle: Passthrough gives up (media never enters LiveKit):

lost.webrtc: No WebRTC / sub-second playback — HLS only (~2 segments of latency).
lost.abr: No adaptive bitrate (ABR) — a single passthrough rendition.
lost.h264: No server-side transcode safety net — the source MUST be H.264/AAC.
lost.recording: No egress recording / VOD for this ingress.
lost.room: No room features (viewer count, chat, reactions, moderation, snapshots, track plugins).
lost.backup: No backup/failover key and no GPU acceleration.

passthrough.disabled503: RTMP/SRT/MPEG-TS passthrough is disabled on this server. Enable STREAMHUB_RTMP_PASSTHROUGH_ENABLE and open the passthrough ports (:1937+ — TCP for RTMP, UDP for SRT; the MPEG-TS udp:// port for multicast), then try again.
passthrough.mpegtsForced: MPEG-TS / UDP only works in passthrough.

note.udp: SRT is UDP — open the ingress port as UDP on the firewall (RTMP passthrough uses TCP).
note.latency: Adds an SRT receive-latency budget (~120 ms by default) on top of the HLS latency.
note.credential: The stream key travels as streamid in the push URL — the key IS the credential; no user/password applies.

mpegts.sourceHint: Required. udp://@GROUP:PORT for multicast (e.g. udp://@239.1.1.1:5000) or udp://@:PORT for unicast. The group must be in 224.0.0.0/4.
mpegts.sourcesHint: Source-specific multicast (IGMPv3): comma-separated source IPs to receive from. Multicast only.
mpegts.localaddrHint: Local NIC IP to join the group on — for multi-homed hosts.
mpegts.fifoHint: UDP receive buffer in 188-byte packets (default ≈ 5.4 MB). Raise it for bursty / high-bitrate multicast.

note.pull: This is a PULL — the server connects OUT to the udp:// source; there is no push URL and no stream key.
note.multicast: For multicast, open UDP for the group/port and make sure IGMP/PIM routing reaches this host.
note.ssm: For source-specific multicast (SSM), list the sender IPs in SSM sources (IGMPv3).
